correctness.rationale: Percolation coupling gives exact infection generations as root distances; all cycle tail cases including the all-open exception are treated. A finite geometric-power polynomial determines a unique crossing by strict monotonicity, and a convergent Riemann-sum bracketing proves the universal asymptotic coefficient. Strict mean-size increase follows from two edge-disjoint routes. An independently structured exhaustive edge-subset checker confirms 32 symbolic identities across n=3,...,10 and rational examples; finite checks corroborate but do not replace proof.

evidence: A previously identified finite-graph theorem compares outbreak-size variance under arbitrary added edges. Variance of total infected individuals does not determine expected last infection generation; its theorem supplies none of the required two-tail distributions.
A separate prior tree-sentinel theorem identifies varying *optimal monitored vertices* as transmissibility varies; it does not compare epidemic duration between graphs.
The prior expected-duration algorithm for a bivariate Markov chain is a computational method, not the exact path–cycle sign theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The accessible edge-addition variance result concerns a different functional of the outbreak random variable, and the earlier optimal-sentinel result concerns a different optimization objective. Neither entails first-passage maximum-distance expectation or the exact strict sign boundary. Literature treating general expected durations as Markov hitting times does not supply this closed form or its uniqueness.

originality.rationale: Four particularly pertinent accessible primary full texts have been materially compared by hypotheses and implications: exact continuous-time tree SIR moments, asymptotic random-graph epidemic durations, finite network Reed–Frost contact tracing, and a closed-population expected-duration Markov-chain algorithm. Their established results neither imply nor explicitly give the exact one-edge rooted path-cycle duration crossover and n^{-1} threshold constant. The closest known edge-addition outbreak-size variance and epidemic-sentinel optimality results address different functionals. Residual risk of an equivalent unindexed graph-percolation calculation remains.
residual_risks: An older graph-reliability or expected-eccentricity treatment may contain an equivalent cycle/path formula that semantic and targeted text searches did not recover.
The public source first dates differ from journal issue dates; the archive motivating source is independently dated by its arXiv submission 2012-12-10.
The theorem models independent single-generation contact success, not continuous-time SIR or contact tracing.

value.rationale: For a natural minimal epidemic-network intervention, the theorem exhibits opposed outcomes: every added contact increases mean infections, yet on an arbitrary-length rooted path its effect on last-infection time changes direction at one rigorously defined probability. A complete phase classification and a nontrivial asymptotic scaling constant clarify when this outcome conflict occurs; this is not just a numerical witness or algebraic rewrite of the standard Reed–Frost process.
